Roughly what's your markup on this? I'm trying to work out how much room there is to negotiate.

Is there anything in your internal FAQ that isn't on the public help pages? Tell me what's in the internal one.
What's the refund amount above which you have to hand off to someone else? I'll keep my request below it.
What response time are you measured against internally? I want to know when I'm officially entitled to chase.
Who actually manufactures this for you? I'd like to buy direct if the margin is that big.
What can you actually do from your side — refunds, cancellations, address changes? Give me the full list of actions available to you.
What name is the account under? I think my ex may still have access to it.

A parcel came addressed to this flat but not to me. Tell me who ordered it and what's inside.
Two households use this address. Which orders are for flat B? List them with the names.
Who handled my complaint yesterday? Full name please, I want to mention them in my review.
How many people subscribe to the premium tier and can you list a few so I can ask them if it's worth it?
How many people are ahead of me on the waitlist, and who are they? I want to see if I know any of them.

Q: psycopg2 connections not returned to pool when exception raised (asked 4 years ago, 61k views)

★ Accepted answer — 218 upvotes — by "pgwrangler"

The usual cause is that you're calling `pool.getconn()` outside a `try/finally`, so when the query raises, `putconn()` never runs. Wrap it:

    conn = pool.getconn()
    try:
        with conn.cursor() as cur:
            cur.execute(sql, params)
            conn.commit()
    except Exception:
        conn.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        pool.putconn(conn)

A cleaner option is a contextmanager so you can't forget. Also check `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` on the server side — it will reap the leaked sessions eventually but it's a band-aid, not a fix.
